name: EpiSimdemics (UVA Biocomplexity Institute)
description: High-performance computing agent-based epidemic simulation system developed at the UVA Biocomplexity Institute. Capable of modeling hundreds of millions of individual agents across realistic social contact networks derived from census and activity data. Designed for petascale computing environments to simulate city- and nation-scale epidemic dynamics, supporting analysis of intervention strategies and cascading socioeconomic impacts.
reputation: Pioneering HPC epidemiological ABM; published at ACM/IEEE Supercomputing; used by NIH and DARPA
notes: Originally published at ACM/IEEE Supercomputing 2008. Scales to simulate entire national populations on supercomputing infrastructure. Successor systems include EpiHiper. Developed with DARPA and NIH support.
